name: Agamaggan's Agility
summary: In Camp Taurajo, Mangletooth offers travelers a blood shard ritual. The captive quilboar channels the power of his ancient boar god, blessing those who bring him shards from the Barrens with swift movement and sure aim.

sections.title: The Power of Blood Shards
sections.body: Crimson blood shards jut from the Barrens soil, especially near quilboar encampments and colossal brambles. Quilboar tradition says the crystals formed from Agamaggan's spilled blood. The Great Boar Ancient fell fighting the Burning Legion in the War of the Ancients. Even locked in a wooden cage at Camp Taurajo, the elder quilboar Mangletooth knows how to channel the stones' dormant divine power for anyone who brings them.

sections.title: Blessing of the Boar Scouts
sections.body: Quilboar hunters and scouts prize ruthless accuracy and blinding quickness in the scrublands. For four blood shards, Mangletooth calls on the fallen demi-god's latent energy, lending the petitioner the instincts and supple grace of his people's best stalkers. He grunts with disdain at outsiders, yet honors his pact and weaves Agamaggan's power into a temporary mantle of agility.

faq.answer: Mangletooth, a Razormane quilboar, offers the ritual from a cage at Camp Taurajo in the southern Barrens. Though the Horde keeps him captive, he bargains with travelers who bring him blood shards.

Blood shards are crystalline stones found throughout the Barrens. They are gathered chiefly from slain quilboar and mineral outcrops near thorn thickets. Quilboar lore says they formed millennia ago when the blood of the Great Boar Ancient Agamaggan drenched the earth.

faq.q: Why is a captive quilboar helping Horde members?
faq.answer: Mangletooth serves his god, Agamaggan, and seeks to survive. He snorts at non-quilboar, yet trades Agamaggan's blessings for blood shards, handling his deity's sacred essence from inside an enemy cage.

faq.q: Can you receive this blessing more than once?
faq.answer: Yes. You can receive the blessing again by bringing Mangletooth four fresh blood shards. He invokes the Great Boar's blessing anew each time.

Agamaggan was a colossal boar Ancient who walked Kalimdor in the ancient mythic era. During the War of the Ancients ten thousand years ago, he fought and fell against the demons of the Burning Legion. His blood nourished the Barrens, giving rise to its impenetrable razor thorns and the quilboar race.

faq.q: What other blessings does Mangletooth provide?
faq.answer: Mangletooth offers rites honoring other aspects of Agamaggan as well. For blood shards, he can bless you with greater physical strength, intellectual wisdom, faster running, or skin as thick as razorhide.

angles.text: As a rogue, you may hear Mangletooth scoff at the speed of non-quilboar rogues. His ritual lets you turn the beast's sacred speed against the tribes of the scrublands.
As a hunter, you value unerring aim and swift stalking, prized virtues for sharpshooters crossing Kalimdor's open expanses.
As a tauren, you respect the Ancients who died in the War of the Ancients. Bargaining with a caged quilboar in Taurajo may still feel uneasy.

As a member of the Horde, you find Mangletooth kept at Camp Taurajo, where Horde forces tolerate his presence and blood shard bargains because the boar god's residual power aids their hard-fought campaign across the Barrens.
